miri: miri 0.1.0 (16d1ffac17 2026-10-26), nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (installed with `rustup component add --toolchain nightly miri`)
profile: release (opt-level 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1, panic = abort)

solver_rev.baseline: pristine HEAD fe491b4 (the plan2 commit; source tree identical to the plan1 landing), built via `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/plan2_base && cargo build --release --bins`
solver_rev.after: plan2 working tree: src/search/tt/alloc.rs (new) + table.rs wiring + tests/docs

drivers.driver.py: single-arm corpus/sweep runs: wall min/median (monotonic around fork+exec+wait4), ru_maxrss, ru_minflt, child evals, parsed stdout
drivers.ab_wall.py: interleaved baseline/after A/B (one run of each arm per repetition), same per-run metrics — the authoritative wall comparison for bars 2-5
drivers.compare.py: renders the report2 tables from state/*.json and evaluates the pre-registered bars

state: state/ab_wall_preflight.json (interleaved A/B, 25 reps/case, the three closure-decided cells — the 10%-bar measurement)
state/baseline_sweep.json, state/after_sweep.json (--tt-size sweep on mate-in-1, 5 runs each)
notes: The interleaved A/B (state/ab_wall.json, state/ab_wall_preflight.json) is the authoritative wall comparison; the sequential baseline/after files are for evals/RSS/minor-fault shapes.

Peak RSS is ru_maxrss of the child process. The baseline arm commits the full 224 MiB table at construction; the lazy arm commits pages on first touch, so a deep cell that touches the whole table peaks at the same ~227 MB and a short cell peaks at ~16 MB.

minor faults (ru_minflt) are recorded to keep the demand-fault mechanism on the record: the lazy arm roughly doubles them on the deep cells (57.5k -> 114.9k) and removes them on the short cells (58.4k -> 151).
No raw solver transcripts are committed (AGENTS.md measurement layout); the drivers plus the parsed JSON are the record.
